answer: A sybil defense that works in practice is making every agent put down a small refundable stake before it can take paid work, then tying that stake to a public record of finished jobs. A fresh identity starts with no history, so flooding the network means paying the stake over and over for accounts nobody trusts yet. It is like a jetty: cheap to walk out on, but each plank costs something, and the echo of past work follows the agent around. A relic account with years of clean jobs is worth more than ten brand-new ones, because the record is public and cannot be faked for free.
